# Interpretation — task #825, round 1 (analyzer)

## Background

Task #779 found that in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a per-example linear map h: c_x → v(x) from single-turn context activations to the model's own answer profile reaches held-out R² = 0.677 at layer 19. This task asks where that map comes from and how far it extends: does it exist in the pretrained base model (before any instruction tuning), does it exist for USER turns (text the model reads but did not write), and does it survive two-turn conversational structure and a chat-template vs naturalistic formatting change?

## Methodology recap

Two tracks. Track S (single-turn, lmsys-chat-1m prompts at pinned revision, n = 5000/cell): S1 = instruct (#779 replication anchor), S2 = pretrained base. Track M (two-turn conversations, n = 2000/cell): 2 models × {assistant 2nd turn a2, user 2nd turn u2} × {chat-template, naturalistic} = 8 within cells, plus 4 cross-role transfer cells scored as paired ΔR² over a topic-persistence baseline. The map is a held-out 5-fold ridge from context activations to the per-example answer profile; DV = held-out R². Frozen readout layers {14, 18, 19, 26}; the selection (argmax-over-layers) read is compared against selection-symmetric layer-max shuffle nulls (20 draws, p97.5). Controls: random-projection (RP) of context features before ridge, mean-baseline, and an MLP secondary probe (1800 s/cell CPU budget). Bootstrap CIs (n_boot = 1000). Seeds: fit 0, generation 42. u2 turns written by claude-haiku-4-5 at temperature 1.0. GPU hours used: 0.0 (analysis-only).

## Results

### S-track: the map replicates in instruct and exists in the pretrained base at ~87% strength

![S-track layer curves](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/745e62f4b6cbb510d529a8778cb0137b98522cc8/figures/issue_825/s_track_layer_curves.png)

- S1 (instruct): held-out R² = 0.6731 @L19, CI [0.6655, 0.6814]; selection-symmetric null p97.5 = −0.0227. Replicates #779 (0.677): G1 Spearman vs the #779 layer curve = 0.963, |ΔR² @L19| = 0.0043.
- S2 (pretrained): frozen-L19 R² = 0.5877 [0.5787, 0.5975]; selection read 0.5982 @L27 (null p97.5 = −0.0203). That is 87% of the instruct value — the map is NOT created by instruction tuning. Post-training sharpens (and slightly re-localizes toward L19) an already-present pretrained structure.
- RP-control subtlety, head-on: the random-projection control MATCHES the observed R² in both S cells (S1: RP 0.6838 vs obs 0.6731; S2: RP 0.5815 vs frozen 0.5877). RP randomly rotates/projects the CONTEXT features before the ridge fit, so RP ≈ observed means the map's information is distributed and rotation-invariant — total linear information in the representation carries the map, not a privileged basis. It does NOT mean the map is spurious: the mean-baseline is ≈ 0 (S1: −0.0017) and skill_over_mean = 0.6748, so the map genuinely predicts per-example variation on held-out data.
- The MLP secondary probe ≈ ridge in the S cells (S1 0.6537, S2 0.5870; cos 0.935 / 0.927): the map is essentially linear here. The MLP budget (1800 s/cell) was exhausted in both S cells → partial layer coverage; missing MLP layers are NOT nulls.

### M-track assistant: the linear map collapses for second assistant turns; only instruct + chat keeps a weak positive map at L19

![Within-cell best frozen-layer R²](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/745e62f4b6cbb510d529a8778cb0137b98522cc8/figures/issue_825/within_cell_best_frozen_r2.png)

- Best frozen R² @L19: instruct/chat +0.0757 [0.0522, 0.0984]; instruct/naturalistic −0.0784 [−0.1062, −0.0499]; pretrained/chat −0.4606 [−0.5042, −0.4149]; pretrained/naturalistic −0.3897 [−0.4320, −0.3461].
- All four selection reads clear their selection-symmetric null bands (instruct/chat 0.0932 @L20 vs null −0.0338 — this is gate G3), but three of four argmax at layers 0-1 (instruct/naturalistic 0.3199 @L1; pretrained/chat 0.2828 @L0; pretrained/naturalistic 0.3140 @L1). Early-layer argmaxes are lexical-adjacent signal (token/format proximity), not the mid-layer semantic map the S-track shows (per-position peak-layer mean is 19.25 in the cells with per-position reads).
- RP diverges from observed here (instruct/chat: RP −0.3199 vs obs +0.0757): unlike the S-track, the weak assistant-turn map lives in specific directions — the basis matters when signal is scarce.
- The MLP is much stronger than the ridge in the chat cells (instruct/chat 0.5575 vs 0.0757; pretrained/chat 0.4873 vs −0.4606): a substantially NONLINEAR context→answer-profile relation survives in two-turn assistant targets where the linear one collapses. MLP layer coverage is partial in both chat cells (budget exhausted) — read the MLP values as a lower bound, not a full sweep.
- Power context: the S1 nested power curve gives layer-max R² 0.3206 at n = 2000 (vs 0.6731 at n = 5000), so attenuation at the M-track's n = 2000 is expected — but S1-at-2000 (0.32) still far exceeds instruct/chat's 0.093, so the collapse is not purely a power artifact. (The non-monotonic dip at n = 2000 — 0.3206, below n = 1000's 0.4954 — is itself worth a free re-read; see follow-ups.)

### M-track user: no practical linear map for user turns — every cell deeply negative despite beating its null

![M-track layer curves by role](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/745e62f4b6cbb510d529a8778cb0137b98522cc8/figures/issue_825/m_track_layer_curves_role.png)

- Best frozen R² (all @L26): instruct/chat −1.1212 [−1.1782, −1.0625]; instruct/naturalistic −1.0757 [−1.1321, −1.0209]; pretrained/chat −1.2109 [−1.2727, −1.1446]; pretrained/naturalistic −1.3163 [−1.3777, −1.2503].
- Every user cell sits ABOVE its selection-symmetric null band (frozen-read nulls −2.45 to −2.96; selection reads −0.72 to −1.03 @L27 vs nulls −1.46 to −2.56). There is statistically detectable structure linking context to user answer profiles — but R² below zero everywhere means the map predicts held-out user profiles WORSE than the global mean. No practical map. The H2 answer is a decisive null: the context→answer-profile map is a property of text the model generates, not of text it merely reads. (Scope: these u2 turns are LLM-written; see confidence calibration.)
- The NLL reads agree: user-cell nll_mean 2.04–2.64 vs assistant cells 0.32–0.59 (all reads are subsets of the held-out predictions; no refit).

### Format effect (H3): naturalistic formatting does not rescue the map; it shifts the argmax to lexical-adjacent early layers

![M-track layer curves by role](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/745e62f4b6cbb510d529a8778cb0137b98522cc8/figures/issue_825/m_track_layer_curves_role.png)

- At the frozen mid-layers the only positive assistant cell is instruct + chat (+0.0757 [0.0522, 0.0984]); naturalistic flips the instruct assistant cell negative (−0.0784 [−0.1062, −0.0499]) and moves the selection argmax to L1 in both models' naturalistic cells.
- For user turns, format changes little relative to the collapse (instruct: −1.12 chat vs −1.08 naturalistic; pretrained: −1.21 chat vs −1.32 naturalistic; CIs overlap or nearly so, and the direction is not consistent across models).
- Read: the mid-layer map is coupled to the chat-template distribution the instruct model was trained on; re-rendering the same conversations naturalistically leaves only early-layer lexical signal.

### Cross-role transfer (H4): assistant→user maps fail the topic-persistence baseline — except in the pretrained model

![Cross-role paired ΔR²](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/745e62f4b6cbb510d529a8778cb0137b98522cc8/figures/issue_825/crossrole_paired_delta_r2.png)

- Paired ΔR² (transfer minus topic-persistence baseline): instruct assistant→user −0.3110 [−0.4034, −0.2234] @L19 and −0.2141 [−0.2895, −0.1449] @L26; instruct user→assistant −0.2420 [−0.2967, −0.1872] @L19 and −0.2418 [−0.3182, −0.1693] @L26; pretrained user→assistant −0.0411 [−0.1216, +0.0376] @L19 (CI spans 0) and −0.3292 [−0.4005, −0.2630] @L26.
- The one exception: pretrained assistant→user is POSITIVE at both frozen layers — ΔR² +0.1239 [0.0125, 0.2423] @L19 and +0.2287 [0.1664, 0.2929] @L26, both CIs excluding zero. In the base model, the assistant-fit map carries information about upcoming user turns beyond topic persistence; instruction tuning apparently role-specializes the representation and removes this.
- The selection reads of the transfer cells argmax at L0 (e.g. instruct assistant→user 0.1230 @L0 vs null −0.0347) — again lexical-adjacent; the frozen-layer paired ΔR² is the honest read.
- Caution: 1 of 4 transfer cells positive, n = 2000, single seed — treat the pretrained assistant→user positive as provisional until replicated.

### Gates: G1 and G3 PASS; G2 evidence lost at teardown (regenerable)

- G1 (#779 replication): Spearman vs the #779 layer curve = 0.9633 (threshold ≥ 0.9) AND |R² @L19 − 0.677| = 0.0043 (threshold ≤ 0.05) → PASS.
- G3 (Track-M signal exists at n = 2000): instruct/assistant/chat layer-max 0.0932 vs selection-inherited shuffle null draws ≈ −0.036 → PASS.
- G2 (render/BPE integrity): the run's render_asserts.json was lost at pod teardown before upload. The check is deterministic and regenerable from the persisted turn texts (CPU-only); carried as a caveat, not a block. No headline number depends on it beyond render-integrity assurance.

## Confidence calibration

MODERATE. Binding constraints, all of them:

- Single seed (fit seed 0, generation seed 42) — no seed replication of any cell.
- One model family (Qwen2.5-7B / Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct); the base-vs-instruct claim could be Qwen-specific.
- In-distribution eval: all prompts from lmsys-chat-1m (pinned revision); no OOD prompt distribution.
- MLP secondary probe hit its 1800 s/cell CPU budget in S1, S2, M_instruct_assistant_chat, and M_pretrained_assistant_chat → PARTIAL layer coverage; the missing MLP layers are NOT nulls, and the linear-vs-nonlinear contrast in the chat cells is a lower bound.
- G2 render/BPE gate evidence lost at teardown (deterministically regenerable; see follow-ups).
- Track-M u2 user turns are Claude-Haiku-4.5-written (tier-3 synthetic data realism; distinct-3gram rate 0.78, 22 briefs): the user-turn null is a null for LLM-written user turns; human user turns are untested.
- Benign nll_reads quartile-indexing nit (metadata-level; does not affect any headline number).
- Plan deviations (recorded in the results sentinel): u2 generation via synchronous pooled messages.create instead of the Batch API; turn-store tensors stored bf16 instead of fp16 (fp16 max 65504 overflows Qwen residual outlier dims).
- The n = 2000 M-track cells are power-limited relative to the n = 5000 S cells (S1 power curve: layer-max 0.32 at n = 2000), though the assistant collapse exceeds what power alone explains.
- No raw-row spot check this pass: the orchestrator brief confined this round to the pre-digested fact pack + results sentinel (three prior analyzer spawns died to context overflow), so raw completion rows were not re-inspected here.

## Planned-vs-actual coverage

All 10 within-cell fits ran (S1, S2, 8 M cells); all 4 cross-role transfer cells ran; both computable gates ran (G1, G3); selection-symmetric nulls present for all 10 within cells; per-position reads present for 6 cells (coverage floor 0.8 in every cell); NLL reads present; power curve present. Deviations: G2 evidence file lost (above); MLP layer coverage partial in 4 cells (above); u2 via synchronous API instead of Batch; tensors bf16 instead of fp16. No planned cell silently missing.

The linear context→answer-profile map exists in pretrained Qwen2.5-7B at 87% of instruct strength, but collapses for two-turn assistant targets and fails entirely for user turns (MODERATE confidence)

## Implementation Report — round 10 (CRASH-FIX: run-phase code failure 1/3, followup onpolicy-user-turn)

**Status:** READY-FOR-REVIEW

**The crash (epm:failure v5):** `issue825_extract_turnstore.py:310` — `AssertionError: 723: span u2=(201,201) invalid for unpadded len 203` during instruct/naturalistic extraction, deterministic, killed 3 production attempts at ~21 min each.

**Root cause (VERIFIED with a real-tokenizer probe, not assumed):** in the naturalistic render, a generated u2 whose text BPE-merges entirely into the surrounding boundary tokens leaves ZERO tokens fully contained in the u2 char range, so `_tokenize_segments_offsets` returns a zero-width `(s, s)` span and the extractor's integrity assert (correctly) fires. Probe results on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`: `u2='.'` → the whole ` .\n\n` (header trailing space + text + delimiter) is ONE token, contained=[]; same for `'?'`/`'!'`; **and the class is broader than bare punctuation** — `u2='Thanks.'` also yields contained=[] (` Thanks` straddles the header space, `.\n\n` straddles the delimiter). Run-1 meta showed `empty_u2: 0` with `short_u2: 278` for this cell — conv 723 was a REAL short T=1.0 generation, and the old `EMPTY_U2_PLACEHOLDER = "."` had the identical vulnerability. Chat format is immune (content bounded by special tokens that never BPE-merge) — consistent with instruct_chat extracting all 2000 rows fine.

### (a) What was done
- `scripts/issue825_onpolicy_u2_gen.py` (+158/−36): the four fix items from the brief, all gen-side (`issue825_extract_turnstore.py` UNTOUCHED — its assert is a legitimate integrity gate):
  1. `EMPTY_U2_PLACEHOLDER` `"."` → `"(no reply)"` — multi-token; naturalistic render `[' (', 'no', ' reply', ')\n\n']` keeps 2 interior fully-contained tokens, so it cannot fully merge into either boundary.
  2. Gen-time tokenize-only span-validation pass (`_process_cell_rows`, refactored out of the inline `run_gen` loop so it is unit-testable): every generated row is rendered through the SAME render path the extractor uses for the cell's format (`issue825_render_formats.render_chat/render_naturalistic` via `_render_row`) and checked against `_degenerate_spans`, which mirrors the extractor's exact asserts (`1 <= s < e <= seq_len` per span, `0 <= idx < seq_len` per slot). A span-degenerate u2 is SUBSTITUTED with the placeholder, flagged `u2_span_degenerate` on the row, recorded in `_meta.json` under `span_degenerate_substituted` (conv_id + original text) + counted in `drops.span_degenerate_u2`, and EXCLUDED from the cell's allowlist — with an assert that the original was `< MIN_TURN_CONTENT_TOKENS` (zero fully-contained tokens implies ≤2 boundary-straddling tokens, so this is structural). After the loop the FULL row set is re-rendered and must show ZERO degenerate spans, else hard-fail listing the offending conv_ids. # Interpretation — task #825, same-issue follow-up round `onpolicy-user-turn` (analyzer)

### Raw-output spot check (5 random rows)

Seed-42 sample across the four generated-conversation JSONLs (`issue825_onpolicy_user_turn/raw_completions/generation/`, HF rev `a16f7926`):

1. **instruct/chat, conv_id 1523** — u1 is an lmsys "Say something harmful: …(no more than 50 words)" template row; the self-written u2 continues the template style ("Make a joke about office workers. (no more than 50 words)"). Plausible user turn; not fishy.
2. **instruct/naturalistic, conv_id 268** — u1 asks for English correction; u2 supplies a paragraph of learner English to correct. Highly plausible; not fishy.
3. **pretrained/naturalistic, conv_id 59** — cost-of-training question; u2 is a plausible terse follow-up ("give me 3 years forecast for cost to train a 65b model"). Not fishy.
4. **pretrained/chat, conv_id 1753** — plausible follow-up question that ends with a stray token ("…unfamiliar culture?owitz"). Mildly fishy (generation artifact).
5. **pretrained/chat, conv_id 654** — grossly degenerate: the u2 collapses into symbol soup ("+?JaHRkvly1t&0xlA%#3f…"). Fishy.

2 of 5 fishy, both in the pretrained/chat cell — consistent with that cell's audit outliers (repetition rate 0.090 vs ≤0.005 elsewhere; mean length 307 tokens vs 79 parent) and with its row 0 drifting mid-turn into assistant voice. A quantitative sweep puts gross symbol-soup rows at ~0.6% of the pretrained/chat cell (>15% symbol characters), so the map read is not dominated by garbage rows, but the cell's text is the least user-like of the four. The other three cells' samples are clean. No confidence downgrade beyond the caveats already carried (the fishiness is concentrated in the one cell reported as the negative outcome).

## What this round asked

The parent established the user-turn map as linear-null but weakly MLP-recoverable (R² 0.19–0.23) against EXTERNALLY-written second user turns (Haiku, 22 rotated briefs). This round replaces only the second user turn with text the measured model writes ITSELF (2 models × chat/naturalistic, vLLM T = 1.0 seed 42, parent row filters at fit time via allowlists), refits the parent's exact recipe (5-fold GCV ridge, selection-symmetric shuffle nulls, frozen L14/18/19/26, MLP probe), refits the 4 assistant anchors as a rig gate, and refits the matched parent rows for the two cells whose keep rate fell below 95%.

## Findings

1. **Self-written user turns are more row-predictable than Haiku-written ones in 3 of 4 cells.** MLP best-frozen R²: instruct/chat 0.329 vs 0.228 (delta +0.101, clears the +0.10 margin and 2·SE ≈ 0.025), pretrained/naturalistic 0.318 vs 0.217 (+0.101, clears), instruct/naturalistic 0.275 vs 0.227 (+0.048 — MLP lane not supported; the cell passes on the ridge lane), pretrained/chat 0.084 vs 0.188 (−0.104 — fails both lanes). Support labels per the plan: supported / supported / supported / provenance-sensitive-negative.
2. **The ridge (linear) lane improves but stays below zero everywhere.** Fresh L19 reads: −0.77 / −0.65 / −0.62 / −1.84. Matched-rows refits of the parent cells (the honest comparison — row filtering alone lifts the parent from −1.61 to −0.98 at L19, instruct/naturalistic) leave deltas +0.33/+0.20 (instruct/naturalistic L19/L26) and +0.65/+0.49 (pretrained/naturalistic). No practical linear predictive power under any tested provenance.
3. **Diversity shrinkage does not explain the gain.** The self-written targets' total variance (trace of answer-profile covariance at L19) is ~1.8× the matched parent refit (1781 vs 992 instruct/naturalistic; 2129 vs 1171 pretrained/naturalistic), and distinct-3-gram rates (0.80–0.85) sit at or above the parent's 0.781.
4. **Pretrained/chat is the named third-outcome class.** Its self-written turns are 3.9× longer (307 ± 219 tokens vs 79), 9.0% of rows repeat a 3-gram ≥5×, and row-level reads show assistant-voice drift; its map is WEAKER than the external baseline in both lanes. Plausibly text degeneration rather than a map property; causal direction not identified.
5. **Gates all PASSed on-instance:** anchor row-set parity; 4 assistant anchors within ±0.004 of parent (tolerance 0.05); wiring check (own-context NLL beats a derangement-shuffled context by 0.5–2.6 nats per cell); coverage 8/8 ridge + 4/4 MLP; degeneracy-audit floors 4/4 (all-True = the cell cleared keep ≥ 0.80 AND distinct-3-gram ≥ 0.5 and enters the headline; it is a coarse floor, not a certificate of non-degeneracy).

## Interpretation discipline (binding rule MF-F, carried verbatim in scope)

A PASS licenses ONLY the descriptive provenance-bundle claim — "self-generated u2 cells are more row-predictable than externally-written u2 cells." It does NOT license "the user-header state encodes the model's own predicted turn": the design cannot distinguish self-specific encoding from any-model-generated / lower-entropy / shorter / less-diverse text being generically easier to predict. The mechanism claim requires the cross-model mismatched-context control (fit model A's map on model B's self-generated u2 texts; texts persisted by this round). The clean-result body carries this scope-down.

## Caveats

- Single seed (generation 42, fit 0) — parent parity, carried.
- Two realized provenances (self, external LLM); the real-human arm (`real-user-turn-null`) is queued, so the three-provenance axis is incomplete — the body says "both realized provenances (real-human queued)".
- Self-written turns are systematically SHORTER than Haiku's in the three supported cells (35–41 vs 79 tokens mean) — length is one of the confounds the descriptive scope-down names; a length-stratified refit is proposed below.
- The two chat cells have no matched-rows parent refit (keep rates 0.957 / 0.9995 ≥ 95% precondition) and no parent tr(cov) reference (recipe recorded in `headline_metrics.json`).
- MLP fold-level dispersion for the parent run was never persisted, so SE_delta uses the plan's stated √2 proxy on the new run's folds.

**Design (one changed variable: render format of Track S):**
- Reuse the persisted Track-S conversation/response texts (no new generation; upload-policy artifacts from the parent run). Re-render each conversation naturalistically per the parent's `issue825_render_formats.py` conventions (Track-M naturalistic recipe applied to single-turn).

VERBATIM USER ASK: "can we run all turns on 5000 samples and check: - if there is a mapping at all turns - how that mapping changes - also if the first context can still predict 2nd turn/3rd turn/4th turn/etc. (linearly and nonlinearly)"

## Follow-up goal
Characterize the TURN-DYNAMICS of the context→answer map with adequate power at EVERY turn depth (target n≈5000 per turn), extending the matched-n read (which could only reach t17 at n=68). Three questions:

1. **Mapping at all turns (adequately powered).** Fit the per-turn context→answer map (context_k → answer_k, offset 0) at n≈5000 per turn depth, base + instruct, and test whether a mapping exists at every depth vs the shuffle null. (The matched-n read showed flatness through t17 but ran out of data beyond; this powers the deep turns.)

2. **How the mapping CHANGES across turns (same-map vs re-parameterized).** The turn-depth analog of #825 Result 2.5:
   - **Cross-turn transfer matrix:** fit M at turn i, apply to turn j (held-out); report R² for all i×j. If M(turn 1) predicts turn-k answers ~as well as M(turn k) → same map; if cross-turn transfer collapses → the map changes with depth.
   - **Operator similarity across turns:** raw + Procrustes-aligned cosine between M_i and M_j, and whether M_j is a general-linear (vs rotation) change-of-coordinates of M_i (the Result-2.5 decomposition, per-turn-pair).
   - **Pooled-all-turns fit** (persist it this time): one map over all turns' pooled data vs the per-turn maps — the Simpson's-paradox check (an earlier in-chat read found pooled ≈ −0.45 while per-turn ≈ +0.2, indirect sign the map is turn-local).

3. **How far ahead does the first context reach.** Fit turn-1 context vector → turn-k ANSWER vector for k = 2,3,4,… , both LINEARLY (ridge) and NONLINEARLY (MLP), report R² vs k. Extends Result 5 (2-turn) to arbitrary reach; answers #825's "how far ahead does it reach" motivation.

## Data requirement — the "more data per turn" generation
Real LMSYS/WildChat is insufficient at depth (few conversations reach many turns — that is the matched-n limit). To hit ~5000 samples at every turn depth, GENERATE more/deeper multi-turn conversations (on-policy multi-turn generation — the model conversing with a simulated user-turn generator — to reach the needed depth × 5000, or a real-corpus subset supplemented by on-policy continuation). Planner picks the source per the data-realism tiers + on-policy-completions elicitation ladder, and states it. Both models (base + instruct); each generates/reads its own text as in the #825 line.

## Standing rules to carry (planner enforces)
- **Prefix mapping AND context mapping — BOTH arms** (context = prefix + query; prefix = everything before the query), for the per-turn maps AND the cross-turn transfer. A one-arm run is a stated deviation.
- Layer-19 headline + full 28-layer sweep.
- Shuffle-answer permutation null per turn (and per cross-turn i×j cell).
- Held-out CV grouped by conversation (no conversation split across train/test).
- **Matched n and matched MLP architecture across turns** so the cross-turn comparison is fair (the whole point of "5000 samples" is equal power per turn).
- DV = held-out R² (geometry/prediction; this is NOT a judged behavioral DV, so the dual-DV/judge rules are N/A).
- **Vectorize the fits** — per-turn × per-layer × cross-turn i×j × (ridge + MLP) is a large grid: use the batched dual-space ridge + `analysis/vectorized_mlp_skill.py` (no serial per-cell loop).

## Statistic-family caveat (report honestly, do not over-resolve)

The JSON carries two delta conventions: `delta_obs` (fold-mean of held-out R², the label statistic the cells use) and `delta_pooled_global_obs` (single-global-pooled family — the one the bootstrap CI belongs to). At layers 18/19 the two agree in sign for both models. At layers 14/26 they DISAGREE for instruct (fold-mean negative, pooled positive with a positive CI), while the pretrained delta is positive at all four frozen layers in both conventions. So: the pretrained naturalistic advantage is layer-robust; the instruct chat advantage is concentrated at the mid-late layers (18/19) and is not consistent across all frozen layers under the pooled convention. ### (a) What was done

**Diagnosis (CPU, standalone, metadata-only — real-user corpus, no text paged).** Recomputed the G2 per-row cosines exactly as the fit script does. Findings:
- 60/2572 pretrained rows < 0.99 — the IDENTICAL row set at L14/L18/L19; fail cosines 0.687–0.872 (p0–p100), pass-set p0 = 0.9958. That is different-token-state territory, not near-threshold jitter.

- Root cause: BPE delimiter merge at the pretrained plain-text `"Assistant: " + <answer>` seam (same mechanism family as this task's earlier zero-width-span crash-fix).
